verdicts.detail: correctly failed on selftest/bad_flow.py:oversped (the same body at 3x the speed: drag goes as v^2 so this is ~9x the force, and the speed was chosen to keep Reynolds inside the same Cd band so the gate fails on the force it measures rather than skipping on validity): drag 88.03 N at 1.65 m/s vs 25.00 N budget (Cd 1.20, A 0.0540 m2, rho 998); Re 9.9e4 turbulent on L 0.060 m, nu from nu; table cylinder_cross (Re 1.0e4-2.0e5, ref D.L; long circular cylinder, flow across the axis)

correctly failed on selftest/bad_flow.py:pinched_bore (the same flow rate through a bore reduced to 60%: at fixed Q the drop goes roughly as 1/D^5, so this is about 12x, and nothing else in the line changes - same length, same roughness, same fittings, same head, same lift): dp 62.91 kPa = major 50.94 + minor 11.97, vs 18.60 kPa budget [from 2.50 m of head less 0.60 m static lift = 1.90 m for friction]; f 0.0242 Colebrook (10 it), Re 2.8e4 turbulent, e/D 1.3e-04, L/D 702, sumK 4.00, v 2.45 m/s (v=Q/A from 0.250 L/s).

correctly failed on selftest/bad_flow.py:transitional_line (the same line at a reduced flow rate that lands Re at the midpoint of the pack's own 2300-4000 transition band, where neither 64/Re nor Colebrook-White holds; geometry, fluid and fittings are untouched and the pressure-drop gate would happily return a confident number. The same fixture carries a positive regression the control cannot express: that this gate settles an external-only flow inside its Cd band instead of skipping on it): REGIME INVALID: internal Re 3.2e3 is in the 2300-4000 transition gap where neither 64/Re nor Colebrook-White holds; change the bore or the flow to leave it | also external Re 3.3e4 turbulent inside cylinder_cross band 1.0e4-2.0e5 | rho 998 kg/m3, nu 1.00e-06 m2/s

correctly failed on selftest/bad_hydrostatics.py:overloaded (the same hull loaded until flotation consumes 1.15x the volume fraction the baseline allows itself; Archimedes is linear in mass so nothing about the geometry moves, and the mass is solved from that stated limit rather than typed): SINKS: 2908.7 kg needs 2.9145 m3 of the 2.8160 m3 watertight volume at rho 998 kg/m3 -> volume fraction 1.035 vs 0.90 limit (-0.0985 m3 reserve buoyancy); this is a VOLUME fraction, not a draft fraction - see fluid.freeboard for draft [T=V/Awp, wall-sided]

correctly failed on selftest/bad_hydrostatics.py:low_deck_edge (the same hull and the same load with the deck edge dropped until freeboard is 1/1.15 of the stated minimum; mass, waterplane and draft are untouched and the watertight volume is re-derived from the new depth so the box stays coherent - only the distance the water has to climb changes): freeboard 0.130 m = depth 0.350 - draft 0.219 at 1120.0 kg, vs 0.150 m minimum [stated min_freeboard_m] [T=V/Awp, wall-sided]

correctly failed on selftest/bad_hydrostatics.py:top_heavy (the same hull with mast-head equipment raising KG until GM is 1/1.15 of the stated minimum; geometry, mass and waterplane are untouched, so BM is identical and only the KG term moves): GM 0.304 m = BM 0.973 - BG 0.669, vs 0.350 m [stated min_gm_m]; positive GM is necessary NOT sufficient - it is the slope at 0 deg only [T=V/Awp, wall-sided]

correctly failed on selftest/bad_hydrostatics.py:masthead_load (KG raised until the arm the hull produces is 1/1.15 of the arm an UNCHANGED heeling moment demands; the demand side is bit-identical to the baseline, so unlike a fixture that scales the moment this one falsifies GZ = GM.sin(theta) itself and not just the float comparison around it): GZ 0.0475 m at 8.0 deg (GM 0.341, BM 0.973), righting moment 522 N.m vs demand 600 N.m; limit 0.0546 m [arm demanded by a 600 N.m heeling moment]; small-angle void past 10 deg [T=V/Awp, wall-sided]

correctly failed on selftest/bad_bounds.py:tall_part (the same part 15% past its stated Z envelope, taken from the projection's own limit; every other number is untouched, so only the height check trips): bbox 96.00x64.00x46.00 vs 100.00x70.00x40.00 mm (worst Z 46.00/40.00 = 115%); vol 94467/110000 mm^3 (86%); com 0.43/1.50 mm off target (28%)

correctly failed on selftest/bad_meshes.py:holed_box (a box with the two triangles of its +Z facet deleted: 4 open edges, winding and every other facet untouched): 4 bad edge(s) across 1 part(s), limit 0 — worst holed_box: 4 open, 0 non-manifold of 10 faces

correctly failed on selftest/bad_meshes.py:flipped_facet (a closed box with one triangle's winding reversed: still watertight, no longer a volume — the case cad.watertight cannot see): 1 of 1 part(s) are not volumes, limit 0 — flipped_box: winding inconsistent

correctly failed on selftest/bad_meshes.py:sliver_pair (one corner of a closed box emitted twice 1e-6 mm apart with a subset of its faces repointed at the copy: adjacency splits on a surface that is still geometrically closed, and the face spanning the two copies has non-zero area until the weld and exactly zero after it): 2 repair(s) needed across 1 part(s), limit 0 — worst split_corner_box: welded 1 vertex/vertices at 0.0001 mm, dropped 1 face(s) below 1e-08 mm^2 over 2 pass(es)

correctly failed on selftest/bad_meshes.py:thin_plate (a plate at a quarter of the project's own minimum wall; the same footprint, watertight, a valid volume, and too thin): thinnest wall 0.625 mm on thin_plate at (5, 5, -0.312) vs 2.500 mm minimum (12/12 inward face-normal rays hit; sampler, not a proof)

correctly failed on selftest/bad_meshes.py:overlapping_pair (two valid 20 mm boxes placed 18 mm apart: 800 mm^3 of shared material, nothing else about either part changed and no allowlist entry): 1 interfering pair(s) of 1 — worst reported 800.000 mm^3 on block_a/block_b vs 0.2 mm^3 / 0.01 mm tolerance: 800.0000 mm^3 vs 0.2 mm^3 tolerance; 2.0000 mm equivalent depth over 400.00 mm^2 vs 0.01 mm

correctly failed on selftest/bad_meshes.py:steep_cone (a cone stood on its apex with a 70-degree half angle: every side face is 70 deg from vertical, well past the limit, and nothing else about the solid is wrong — it is watertight, on the bed, and the right size): worst supportable face 70.0 deg vs 45 deg limit; 64 faces past it covering 3628.8 mm^2 = 51.56% of surface (allowance 0.50%); steepest downward face on the part 70.0 deg, 0 at or past 80 deg excluded as ceilings — they are fdm.bridge_span's

correctly failed on selftest/bad_meshes.py:long_bridge (an arch whose flat ceiling spans three times the limit between two properly anchored legs, so the gate has to measure a real bridge rather than notice a cantilever — the span is the only thing wrong: the solid is watertight, sits on the bed and fits the build volume): worst unsupported span 90.0 mm vs 30 mm limit (BRIDGE, 2 anchored edge(s) around it) on a 3600 mm^2 ceiling at 20.0 mm; 1 ceiling region(s) from 2 faces, bridges judged at 30 mm and cantilevers at 2 mm

correctly failed on selftest/bad_params.py:brim_overflow (a footprint sized halfway between the bed minus its brim and the raw bed — derived from both, so it is always inside the bed and always outside the brimmed area; the one case a naive bed check calls a pass and the printer calls a crash): 215x215x31 mm vs 210x210 usable (220x220 bed - 2x5.0 brim) x 250 Z; as modelled, worst util 1.02 in XY

correctly failed on selftest/bad_params.py:two_perimeter_wall (the same part with its thinnest section cut to two beads of the line width the project actually uses — two perimeters and a seam of gap fill, which prints and then fails in service; nothing else about the part changes): thinnest section 0.84 mm = 2.0 beads vs 1.26 mm minimum (3 x 0.42 mm line width)

correctly failed on selftest/bad_params.py:load_across_layers (the same part rotated so the load runs along the build axis, with the utilisation scaled to sit 15% past the layer-normal knockdown — the one change that turns a passing structural result into a part that snaps along a layer): load at 90 deg to the layer plane (build axis from the model): stress utilisation 0.57 (utilisation) / knockdown 0.50 = 1.15 vs 1.00 (layer-normal strength 0.50x in-plane)

correctly failed on selftest/bad_params.py:crawling_speed (the same part at the speed that puts it 15% past the project's own print-time ceiling — solved from the gate's own model, in the flexible-filament regime; geometry untouched): ESTIMATE ~27.6 h of 24 h, ~39 g of 1000 g (30.7 cm^3 at 35% infill, 3x0.42 mm shell on 20657 mm^2) — 0.20 mm layers at 7 mm/s x 0.55 duty; time is the binding one at 1.15 of its ceiling. Not a slice.

correctly failed on selftest/bad_params.py:metres_not_millimetres (the same part and machine described in metres — every length, area and volume in the projection divided by 1000 to the right power: one physically meaningful change, and every other gate in this pack goes on returning confident answers about it): longest dimension 0.08 — below 1 mm, so the model is almost certainly in metres (80 mm?) and every threshold in this pack is out by 1000x; nozzle 0.0004 mm is outside the 0.25-1.2 mm range this pack's wall and bridging rules were written for — extrapolating them is guesswork, not a measurement

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boms.py:unpriced_line (one line's unit_price blanked out — the single most common real BOM defect. Nothing else about the part changes, and the roll-up that silently treats it as free is exactly what this gate refuses): 1 of 10 lines not orderable (limit 0): HSG-01

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boms.py:price_shock (one line repriced so that part alone costs ten times the whole per-unit budget — the re-quote that arrives the week you order. One number moves; quantities, vendors and charges are untouched): 621.61 USD/unit at qty 500 vs 58.00 USD budget; parts 307,557.30 USD + minimums 275.20 USD + one-time 2,970.00 USD (5.94 USD/unit amortised) = 310,802.50 USD run

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boms.py:end_of_life (one line's lifecycle moved to 'eol' — the notice that arrives by email and gets filed. Price, quantity and vendor are unchanged; only the part's future is): longest lead 12 wk (U2); vs 16 wk budget; 0 unknown, 1 EOL, 1 flagged; EOL: HSG-01; watch: REG-01:nrnd

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boms.py:brutal_moq (one line's MOQ raised far past what the build needs, on the line whose price makes the overbuy real money. The part, the price, the order multiple and the design are unchanged — only the smallest quantity the vendor will sell. The raise is computed from the limits it has to beat, read out of the same document the gate reads them from, so it goes on tripping when a project moves a threshold): idle capital 48,540.50 USD vs 6,999.73 USD (10% of the 69,997.30 parts spend); worst HSG-01: 4600 bought for 500 needed (9.2x) = 46,740.00 USD; 2 line(s) past 3x; worst past the filter HSG-01 46,740.00 USD vs 50.00 USD per-line limit — OVER

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boms.py:outside_capability (one declared process attribute moved outside the vendor's stated set — a finish the quoted line does not offer, or a tolerance ten times tighter than the process holds — written everywhere the document records that one fact, so a design-scoped rule and a line-scoped rule both trip from the single change and neither half of the rule engine goes unexercised. The BOM is otherwise untouched): 2 violation(s) of 7 project-supplied rule(s) (limit 0): board-finish-for-press-fit@design.surface_finish 'levelled-solder' is not one of ['ENIG', 'hard-gold']; fab-class-capability@PCB-01.surface_finish 'levelled-solder' is not one of ['ENIG', 'immersion-tin']

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boms.py:lost_second_source (the second source goes away, with nothing written down — expressed on each line in the terms that line records: the lines that name a MANUFACTURER keep both distributors and lose the qualified alternate (two distributors of one factory's part is the case this gate exists for and the case a distributor count cannot see), the lines that name only suppliers drop to one. Prices, quantities and vendors are untouched. Enough lines to clear whatever single_source_limit the project set, so the control does not stop tripping when somebody raises it): 2 unrecorded single-source line(s) vs limit 0 (3 behind one source in total, 0 with a qualified alternate, 1 accepted in writing): U1 (manufacturer Wexmoor Semiconductor, stocked by 2), REG-01 (manufacturer Wexmoor Semiconductor, stocked by 2); 7 line(s) record no manufacturer, so their sources are counted by supplier — two distributors of one factory's part would read as two there

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boms.py:foreign_quote (one line re-quoted in a currency the document holds no fx rate for — the vendor who sends the second quote on their own price list. The part, the quantity, the vendor and the number itself are unchanged; only the currency beside the number is, which is precisely the change a roll-up cannot see and must refuse): 1 of 10 line(s) priced in a currency this document cannot convert (limit 0): HSG-01 priced in JPY with no fx_rates['JPY'] to reach USD

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boat.py:battery_aft (the 98 g battery moved to the aft end of the equipment bay -- one plausible cable-routing decision, nothing else changed. It is the exact move the fluids lens list warns about ('the battery that gets relocated for cable routing')): trim -1.89 deg (-15.8 mm bow-to-stern) vs 1.50 limit; freeboard 24.9 mm after trim vs 25 mm required (level flotation would have reported 31.6 mm, so trim costs 6.7 mm); LCG 187.9 vs LCB 212.1 mm

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boat.py:top_heavy (mass added on deck, SOLVED for the value that misses this gate's own stated acceptance by 1.15x rather than typed -- a control calibrated to a literal stops being a control the moment the threshold moves. A mast or a light bar is the most common thing added to a finished boat and it always goes up, which is the lens-4 failure exactly): GM 11.1 mm solid, minus 2.4 mm of free surface = 8.7 mm vs 10 mm; the girder divides the bilge into 53 mm cells -- undivided the correction would be 9.6 mm

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boat.py:one_big_bay (bulkheads pushed out to 25 mm and 455 mm, which is the obvious move if you want the biggest possible equipment bay and have not thought about flooding. Nothing else changes; the hull, the mass and the loading are identical): sealed compartments support 188 g against an all-up 1182 g -> -994 g margin with the equipment bay full. Foam-filled, so the reserve fails gracefully rather than closed-loop

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boat.py:top_heavy_empty (same solved topside mass as boat.free_surface's control, which raises KG in the condition where KG is already highest because the battery -- the heaviest low item -- has been taken out): empty GM 8.7 mm (KG 79.5 mm vs 76.8 loaded) at 41.9 mm draft, vs 10 mm

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boat.py:steep_shaft (shaft angle raised to 22 degrees, which is what you reach for when the motor will not clear the hull floor. It is past what a flexible coupler will take and it drags the propeller down into the rudder): shaft angle 22.0 > 12 deg

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boat.py:bugged_offset (the inner offset scaled to half, simulating exactly the class of generator bug this project actually hit. The meshes stay watertight and stay valid volumes, which is the point: every other geometry gate passes a mesh with the wrong wall): worst disagreement 53.4% on hull_bow (0.745 mm from mesh volume/area vs 1.60 mm specified); all shells: hull_aft 0.790, hull_bow 0.745, hull_mid 0.788

correctly failed on selftest/bad_boat.py:oversize_hull (hull_scale 3.0, i.e. a 900 mm boat. Also the units-slip control: a model that has silently gone metres-for-millimetres somewhere fails here loudly instead of exporting a plausible STL nobody measures): assembled 900 x 349 x 159 mm vs 560 x 230 x 170 mm envelope (worst axis 161%)
